summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, cardiomyopathy (multifactorial, including Chagas disease), and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting was admitted for lightheadedness and bradycardia. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia (K 8.0) with EKG changes including peaked T waves and conduction delays. He received emergency treatment with atropine, insulin, dextrose, calcium, and albuterol, followed by hemodialysis, which normalized his potassium and resolved the arrhythmia. His carvedilol, torsemide, and spironolactone were discontinued due to bradycardia and minimal urine output. He remained stable, with improving electrolytes and no recurrence of symptoms, and was discharged home with plans to follow up with cardiology for pacemaker evaluation and nephrology for dialysis management.
